features_title:
From a project file
to a clear picture.
features_intro: You know your installation. Your tools should help you understand it, not get in the way.
feature_one_body: Import supported ETS projects with a report of warnings and limitations. Continue in KNXBench’s own versioned format. Or start a new project from scratch.
feature_two_body: Topology, buildings, devices, group addresses and links in one workbench. With search, an inspector and undo/redo, so the next change stays understandable too.
feature_three_body: Observe telegrams over KNXnet/IP, inspect values and explore communication as a table or flow view. Individual messages become a picture you can follow.
release_title:
Alpha 17.
Explain the refusal. Check before writing.
release_intro: A System-2 path that says why it stopped. A regular download that checks harder before it writes and remembers why it failed. Comparison adoption that can take over association links. Alpha 17 is published as a pre-release, with public downloads and Docker image identities verified.
release_download_title: A regular download that checks first.
release_download_body: Hardware type and application identity must answer with their exact width before any backup or mutation. Backups record the prior application, and a finished download is credited only while the current catalogue still plans the identical download. A failed download keeps one payload-free cause in status, report, history and CLI. Device families and hardware support are unchanged.
release_adoption_title: Association links, adopted with a preview.
release_adoption_body: From a complete, decoded mask-0701h association table, comparison adoption can now take over object ↔ group-address links per whole object, with a preview of the link changes. No group address or object is created, and nothing is written to a device.
release_workbench_body: A device’s Diagnostics tab opens Analyse device and Send report with that device selected. The object table names each object’s saved project folder, the Flow map shows the single unambiguous group name, project history shows native versions on a timeline, and catalogue columns sort on click.
release_system2_body: The experimental configured download for UP 258D12 application M-0001_A-9205-04-9270 now records differing device observations instead of refusing; hardware type, mask version and manufacturer stay hard. A refused table-reference read ends with a typed reason and its counts, while raw bytes stay in the private journal. Tested with simulated and loopback transports only: not physical-device or recovery certification, general System-2 support or ETS parity.
release_more_note: Matrix object columns share one resizable, remembered width. AppImage save and open dialogs start in the launch directory. Project and product ZIP readers refuse contradictory AES metadata; consistent AES stays unsupported.
release_scope_note: Alpha 17 is a published pre-release, not a stable release. GitHub downloads and SHA-256/provider digests are verified. The Docker index for amd64 and arm64 carries the exact release revision; the version and latest tags shared it at readback. The arm64 image was built and published by CI, not run locally.

From Alpha 14.
The workbench in pictures.

watch_title:
Don’t just read about it.
See it.
watch_intro: Short looks at the real application. Every recording uses fictional sample data, not somebody’s actual installation.
project_body: Add a device from the product catalog, assign a free address and link a communication object to a group address. Without jumping between five different tools.
project_transcript: A push button is picked from the product catalog, named “Push button dining” and created with a free individual address in the sample house. Its first communication object is then linked to 0/0/2 “Kitchen light” with the searchable address picker. The recording uses zoom and plays at double speed.
project_caption: Alpha 14 · Real app · Sample house · Zoom, 2× speed
flow_body: The flow view brings senders, receivers and values together. Here it follows lights, blinds and temperature in the sample house, in the optional green CRT theme.
flow_transcript: Simulated telegrams from the fictional sample house make devices appear in the flow view: lights switch on and off, a blind moves down, and temperature and valve values change.
flow_caption: Alpha 14 · Flow view · Fictional sample house
details_body: Filter group addresses, select an address and inspect its properties right beside it. A calm workspace for the details that matter.
details_transcript: The real app shows the sample house’s group addresses. Typing “Kitchen” into the filter narrows the tree; 0/0/2 is selected and its properties and links appear right beside it. The filter is then cleared again.

story_title:
How an idea
became a workbench.
story_body: It began with wanting a KNX tool on Linux. Then came decisions, detours, AI assistants and rather a lot of “just one more thing”. The Evolution Story follows that path, with evidence and a slightly melancholy narrator.
status_title:
Already a workbench.
Still an alpha.
status_body: KNXBench is under active development. Try it, keep backups and check whether your project and devices fit the supported scope. Your feedback helps make the next version better.
status_summary: Project work, product data and bus diagnostics are at the core. Import support and device operations have explicitly documented boundaries: not every format or device has the same level of support.
scope_import: ETS project import is limited to supported formats and versions. Warnings and unsupported content are surfaced in the import report; full ETS compatibility is not promised.
scope_export: After import, you work in .knxdb. Export back to .knxproj is not provided.
scope_hardware: Commissioning and device downloads support limited, documented paths. Project editing does not mean every device can be programmed.
scope_secure: KNX Secure is not currently implemented.
backup_note: Try a copy first. Read the application’s guidance before hardware operations.
demos_title:
A project to explore.
No installation to risk.
demos_intro: Three fictional offline projects for your own KNXBench instance. Each ZIP includes a native .knxdb, the shared fictional product catalogue and an English tour with five exercises.
demos_home_summary: 32 devices, 105 group addresses. Two living floors, basement and outside areas.
demos_residential_summary: 101 devices, 339 group addresses. Six apartments, three living floors and shared areas.
demos_office_summary: 157 devices, 507 group addresses. Three floors with offices, meeting rooms and auxiliary areas.
demos_all: Download all three demos (ZIP on GitHub)
demos_setup: Extract a ZIP and keep an untouched reset copy. Install fictional-demo-devices.knxprod once through Product catalog, then open a copy of the .knxdb via File → Open. Native edits can auto-save.
demos_safety: Offline exploration only. Fictional applications contain no firmware and must never be downloaded to real devices. These projects are not ETS exports or electrical plans.
demos_version_note: Demo version 1.0.0. The frozen ZIP READMEs retain their original “local review candidate” label. See the guide for the tested development build; compatibility with older alpha releases is not promised.
start_title:
The next view
is your own.
start_body: No account with us. No hosted demo. KNXBench runs on your own instance, so you try the real product.
launch_note: The repository and its alpha downloads are public on GitHub. This website itself is still a preview and not published yet.
docker_body: Use the web app through a suitable Docker environment on your system. The container brings the interface and server together; you stay in control of your projects.
docker_step_two: Pull the ready-made image, configure storage and access.
docker_step_three: Open it in your browser, create a project or import a copy.
docker_note: Published for amd64 and arm64, with the exact release revision verified in the registry. Use 0.1.0-alpha.17 to pin this pre-release, or latest to follow published releases including alphas. The arm64 image is CI-built, not run locally. The guide explains live-bus networking; latest does not mean stable.
native_body: The published Alpha 17 x86-64 AppImage packages the desktop application for Linux. Its public download and checksum are verified. The release page has the files; read the linked system requirements and installation guidance before upgrading.
native_note: Choose an alpha version, read the release notes and work with project copies.
support_intro: You don’t have to figure it all out alone.
footer_tagline: An independent workbench for KNX projects.
independence: KNXBench is an independent project. It is not affiliated with the KNX Association and is not KNX certified. KNX and ETS are mentioned to describe the application’s scope.
license_note: Free software under AGPL-3.0-or-later. Free to use, including commercially, subject to the licence terms.
privacy_body: This website uses no analytics scripts, marketing cookies, embedded video services or remotely hosted fonts. Media and fonts load from the same site host. GitHub links lead to an external service.
privacy_pending: Before public launch, information about the actual hosting, possible server logs and privacy enquiries will be added and reviewed. This local preview is not a final privacy notice for the future site.
contact_body: Public project feedback and support gaps can be reported on GitHub in the KNXBench repository, using its support-gap form. Share only information explicitly approved for public disclosure, not confidential projects or credentials.
privacy_hosting: This website is hosted on GitHub Pages, a service of GitHub, Inc. According to GitHub's documentation, the visitor's IP address is logged and stored for security purposes when a GitHub Pages site is visited. For privacy enquiries, use the contact on the legal notice page.
upgrade_note: Before updating: close KNXBench and independently back up .knxdb files, the closed product database and persistent Docker data. Keep original .knxproj/.knxprod files. Alpha 17 keeps native/model schema 16 and product database 28 from Alpha 16; no migration is needed. Alpha 16 refuses Alpha 17’s format-2 device backups and new history and System-2 records rather than dropping them; opening Alpha 17 saves in Alpha 16 is not tested. Coming from Alpha 15, the product database migrates 26 → 27 → 28 on writable open and Alpha 15 refuses product28; there is no catalogue downgrade path. Returning needs your pre-upgrade backup; in-file history is not one.
release_parameters_body: An area register built from the product data, compact aligned rows and one search across every area. Switch areas freely: drafts and conflicts stay exactly where you left them.
release_parameters_alt: Alpha 14 in Graphite: the Parameters tab of the fictional ground-floor switch actuator with its area register, Channel A open and aligned parameter rows.
release_vendor_body: Hand the catalogue the manufacturer’s ZIP: every product package inside is previewed, then installed together, byte for byte — or not at all. Manuals are listed, not hoarded.
release_vendor_alt: Alpha 14 in Graphite: the catalogue update preview of a vendor ZIP holding the fictional demo package and a manual, with nine new products listed before anything is installed.
release_notes_body: Deleting something that notes point at now asks first: keep each note on the project, move it elsewhere or delete it. It all happens in one step, and one Undo brings everything back.
release_notes_alt: Alpha 14 in Graphite: the dialog Notes need a decision for two notes on the new Dining light group address, each offering keep, move or delete.
release_diagnostics_body: The diagnostic export picks one device, shows exactly which identity data it will read, then saves a local ZIP for the maintainers. It only reads — the device stays exactly as it was.
release_diagnostics_alt: Alpha 14 in Graphite: the Export diagnostic data dialog with a selected device, a gateway address and the preview of the planned read-only identity reads.
